text: Every child in our village knew the rule.
Never... leave the path.
The winter I turned seven, my mother tied a red hood under my chin, and gave me a basket for my grandmother.
I didn't have a grandmother. I didn't know that yet.
The path went down into the valley. The deeper it went, the quieter the world became.
Then the wolf came.
And everybody knows what wolves do to little girls.
It chased me off the path, up the ridge, into the deep snow. And then it stopped... and waited.
From up there, I could see where the path ended.
There was a house. There was no grandmother.
Only red hoods. One for every winter.
The village called it Grandmother. They fed it one child a year, so it would leave the rest of them alone.
My mother had packed my basket herself. Bread. Wine.
And a lantern.
She couldn't save me. But she could give me fire.
Every winter, the wolf chased a child off the path.
And every winter, the child ran back.
Because we'd all been taught... never leave the path.
When I walked home, nobody cheered.
They looked at me like I was the monster.
They told every child she was walking to her grandmother's house.
So I became one.
Which path were you told never to leave?
